title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: {P8W48} rings function as reusable porous nodes that transition-metal cations stitch into open all-inorganic lattices, with Ag+ concentration, heating, and pH switching between layered and less dense cubic packings.
explanation: Cronin-type frameworks connect discrete {P8W48} fragments through Mn–O–W, Co, or Ag links. Mn-bridged phases pack as cubic or hexagonal cylinder arrays with nanometer-scale cavities or channels near 10.75 Å. Higher Ag+ with heating fragments and reorganizes the rings, lower Ag+ without heating gives layered Ag-linked stacks, and a pH adjustment yields a less dense cube whose internal cavity is about 2.1 nm and accessible through integrated pores.
scope: Polyoxotungstate all-inorganic frameworks that use {P8W48} as the main SBU and Mn2+, Co2+, or Ag+ as linkers.
conditions: Aqueous Li-buffered or related simple solution conditions; Ag series compared at higher concentration with heating to 80 °C versus lower concentration without heating, plus a pH change.
caveats: Channels are often filled by aqua-metal ions, NH4+, Li+/K+, and solvent, so crystallographic cavity size is not the same as permanent porosity.
